target_customer: Individuals and small teams who want a personal OpenClaw AI agent running in the cloud and connected to Slack or other messengers without self-hosting
problem: Self-hosting the open-source OpenClaw agent takes setup time and security work. Klaus sold a preconfigured, hosted instance with security features and common skills already installed.
business_model: Monthly subscription per hosted instance (Show HN listed $19, $49 and $200 per month tiers with small token credits)
product_category: Managed hosting for an open-source AI agent

founders.name: Robbie Thompson
education: Stanford, MCS student (as listed on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. The page says the founders met building AI agents at Console.

founders.name: Bailey Wickham
founders.background_notes: YC page says the founders previously worked at Amazon and Jane Street and met at Console, without attributing each employer to one person. No individual education listed.

exit.reason: The company site states the service ended on September 1, 2026 and customer assistants were taken offline; no reason is given.

competitors.name: xCloud
competitors.what: Fully managed OpenClaw hosting that handles setup, updates and security

competitors.name: ClawHost
competitors.what: Hosted or deployable OpenClaw offering, described in one comparison as managed from about $29 per month

technical_complexity.rationale: Provisioning a dedicated VM per user with preinstalled keys, OAuth apps and automatic updates is standard cloud engineering. The hard part was security hardening of an agent that holds user credentials.

defensibility.rationale: The product wrapped an open-source project the company does not own. Many hosted OpenClaw competitors appeared within weeks, so copying took days.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Many hosts shipped managed OpenClaw. Anthropic ended subscription access for third-party tools on 2026-04-04 (per a search summary, not specific to Klaus). Klaus shut down 2026-09-01.

market_need_then: OpenClaw went viral in early 2026 and many users wanted a safe hosted setup. Show HN on 2026-03-11 drew discussion. Pricing was low and demand was driven by a fast-moving open-source trend.

branding.domain_note: Operated on klausai.com (name plus ai suffix); acquisition history not found. Legal entity shown in the footer is Usebits Inc.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and direct (hosted OpenClaw that is secure and powerful out of the box)

branding.community_and_virality: Show HN post dated 2026-03-11 with about 91 comments per a showcase mirror; no merch or fan content found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found, and the product borrowed the OpenClaw brand for pull. The name Klaus is a common first name with no tie to the product.

outcome_analysis: Klaus launched hosted OpenClaw in the winter 2026 batch, shipped a Show HN on 2026-03-11 and ended service on 2026-09-01 per its own site. The company gives no cause and no post-mortem or press coverage was found, so the cause of the shutdown is not public. Context that is not tied to Klaus by any source: a crowded set of OpenClaw hosts and Anthropic's April 2026 change to third-party subscription access.
notes: Two funding searches found no round, amount or investor. VCBacked lists Y Combinator with stage Grant and no amount; this is YC's standard deal and is not recorded as a round. Competitor entries rest on a single comparison blog (snippet only, page not opened). One search summary showed Klaus as Active on the YC page; the queue lists Inactive.
